name: Deconstructivism
summary: Skewed, fractured volumes that collide at sharp angles, with a facade that seems to tear itself apart. Gehry, Hadid, Libeskind and Coop Himmelb(l)au used distortion to disturb the pure box of the Modern Movement from inside.

philosophy.core_thesis: The pure form is already flawed: distort the grid, collide the volumes and let the building show that order is unstable.
design_principles: Collide two or more orthogonal volumes at 10 to 40° skews, so that no wall is parallel to its neighbour.
Fragment the form into 5 to 15 shards or bars that overlap, tilt and cantilever.
Tilt walls and floors off the vertical by 3 to 15°, and let beams and columns slope.
Cut slot windows and sharp gashes at angles that do not follow the floor levels.
Show the stress: bracing, folded planes and structure that seems to carry the load without a clear path.
Wrap the shards in one material, usually metal sheet, zinc or titanium, and let the joints draw the geometry.
anti_patterns: Regular orthogonal grids and repeated bays
Soft rounded blob forms with no hard edges
A plain box with one decorative sloped wall
Windows aligned with floor levels and a clear horizontal order

massing.form: Shards, bars and planes that cross and cantilever 3 to 12m; two or more volumes at skewed angles in one composition.
massing.proportion: Long thin elements, with a ratio of 1:6 or more, crossing short stout ones; the silhouette has no clear centre.
massing.roof: A tilted, folded or broken roof that continues the wall; no flat roof with a clear edge line.
massing.relation_to_ground: The mass crashes into or lifts off the ground: a splayed base, a cut-in plaza or a slab that is propped on one point.

structure.system: A steel frame or space-frame, often designed with 3D software, with a concrete core and a sheet-metal skin.
structure.span_and_module: No regular module: spans vary from 4 to 30m and members are cut to a unique length and angle.
structure.expression: The structure is shown as a tangle: raking columns, trusses and braces cross the interior and the skin.

materials.finish: Mixed: bright metal on the shards, raw or plain finish on the inside, and joints that are visible and unaligned.

facade.composition: Overlapping planes at different angles; the window pattern ignores floor levels and the front has no clear base, middle and top.
facade.openings: Slots, triangles and wedges cut at skewed angles, 3 to 20% of a plane at a time; the window-to-wall ratio is 20 to 50%.
facade.solid_to_void: Solid leads at 50–80%, cut by sharp voids.

light_and_space.daylight: Light enters through slashes, skylights and tilted glass; it makes sharp, moving bars and wedges across the floor.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A route with no straight line: slanted halls, split stairs and bridges lead through the shards and show a new view at each turn.
light_and_space.interior_character: Tilted walls, sloped floors, exposed bracing and few right angles; the room has no clear centre.

ornament.attitude: No ornament in the classical sense; the distortion and the fracture are the only expression.

rules.rule: Hold the tension of colliding forms in a fragile balance.
Cut a sharp angle against another at 20 to 70°.
Layer overlapping planes that pierce each other.
Let there be no single focus: let the fracture itself pull the eye.
Draw long diagonal lines that cross the whole mass.

images.title: Vitra Fire Station, Weil am Rhein

emotion.target_response: Unease and thrill: the viewer feels a stable order break up and finds beauty in the break.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a low-cost, repeatable or fast-to-build building.
The programme needs clear, regular rooms, as in housing or a hospital.

modifiers.how: Return the shards to a 6 to 12m grid, keep the exposed structure and the glass, and cut the skew angles to 0° and 90°.

Vitra Fire Station, Weil am Rhein

sources.title: Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley, Deconstructivist Architecture (Museum of Modern Art, 1988)
